filter-numbers.formula:
keep(n): n satisfies the chosen rule
even: n mod 2 = 0 | odd: n mod 2 = 1 (integers only)
prime: exactly 2 factors | divisible by k: n mod k = 0
greater than k: n > k | less than k: n < k
unique: first occurrence kept, later repeats dropped
howTo: Paste or type your numbers into the box, separated by commas, spaces or line breaks.
Pick a rule from the dropdown: keep even, keep odd, keep prime, divisible by, greater than, less than, unique, or sort.
If the rule needs a value (divisible by, greater than, less than), enter it in the second box.
The kept numbers appear instantly, with counts of how many were kept and removed.
Use the copy button to grab the filtered list.
keyFacts: A filter keeps only list members that satisfy a rule and drops the rest.
Even numbers divide by 2 with no remainder; odd numbers always leave a remainder of 1.
Prime numbers have exactly two factors. 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime.
Divisible-by-k keeps every number n where n mod k = 0 - those are the multiples of k.
Remove-duplicates keeps the first occurrence of each value and drops repeats.
Sorting ascending or descending reorders the list without removing any number.
filter-numbers.keywords: filter numbers, keep even numbers, find prime numbers in list, remove duplicates numbers, filter numbers by rule, number list filter
limitations: One rule per run - rules cannot be combined in a single pass.
Even/odd/prime rules ignore decimal numbers, since parity and primality are defined for integers.
Lists longer than 50,000 characters are truncated to keep the page responsive.
This is a quick list tool, not a full spreadsheet - it cannot save or export files.

filter-numbers.quickAnswer: This tool keeps only the numbers in your list that satisfy a rule. From the list 12, 7, 30, 5, 18, 3, the keep-even rule returns 12, 30 and 18 - three numbers kept, three removed. You can also keep odd or prime numbers, keep numbers divisible by any value, keep numbers above or below a threshold, remove duplicates, or sort ascending and descending. Numbers may be separated by commas, spaces or line breaks.
filter-numbers.tagline: Keep or drop numbers from a list by rule - even, odd, prime, divisible, unique, sorted.
filter-numbers.workedExample:
Filter the list 12, 7, 30, 5, 18, 3 with the keep-even rule:
1. Check each number: 12 mod 2 = 0 (keep), 7 mod 2 = 1 (drop), 30 mod 2 = 0 (keep).
2. Continue: 5 mod 2 = 1 (drop), 18 mod 2 = 0 (keep), 3 mod 2 = 1 (drop).
3. Kept: 12, 30, 18. Removed: 7, 5, 3.
4. Result: 3 kept out of 6 total.
